name: ICT security policies, procedures, protocols and tools for resilience, continuity and availability
framework_text_summary: Design and implement ICT security measures ensuring resilience, continuity and availability, and data security at rest, in use and in transit.

gap: Generic article; these checks are illustrative technical measures, not proof of the policy set.

name: Network and infrastructure management, with ability to isolate and segment
framework_text_summary: Risk-based network and infrastructure management; connections can be severed or segmented.
tested: Firewall inspectors that could be read, failed if any row is "bad" (for example support or security subscription expired, HA not configured, health errors, warranty ended). It does not read rules, admin exposure or admin credentials.
gap: Segmentation and isolation capability are not tested. The page maps boundary to 9(4)(c), which is access control.
source: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 (DORA), Article 9. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2022/2554/oj ; text checked via https://www.digital-operational-resilience-act.com/Article_9.html Scope rationale:.

name: Limit physical and logical access; sound administration of access rights
framework_text_summary: Limit access to what is required; policies and controls for access rights.
tested: Accounts disabled in at least one system but still present or holding admin rights in another inspected tool (excluding AD, Microsoft 365, KnowBe4, dark web). Enabled accounts with no sign-in for 90+ days or reported stale by a source; accounts with no sign-in data are named, not passed. Enabled personal accounts that hold a top-level admin role (global admin, super admin, owner, domain admin) instead of a separate admin account.
gap: Physical access not seen; policy is a document.
source: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 (DORA), Article 9. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2022/2554/oj ; text checked via https://www.digital-operational-resilience-act.com/Article_9.html Scope rationale:.

name: Strong authentication and protection of cryptographic keys; encryption by data classification
framework_text_summary: Strong authentication mechanisms and protection of cryptographic keys; encryption based on classification and risk assessment.
tested: Enabled accounts with admin rights in any inspected identity system, and whether each has MFA reported in every system it exists in (Identity & access "Admins without MFA"). MFA here is registration as reported by the source (for Microsoft 365, isMFARegistered, which needs Entra ID P1 and stays "Enabled" after MFA is switched off). Share of enabled people and admin accounts with MFA reported in every system they exist in. Pass at 98% or more, partial at 80% or more. Registration, not enforcement. Open BitLocker or "not encrypted" alerts on Windows devices, plus any current encryption-off finding from other tools. A device with no alert counts as encrypted.
gap: MFA registration; disk encryption alert-based; key management not seen. The page maps encryption to 9(4)(c).
source: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 (DORA), Article 9. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2022/2554/oj ; text checked via https://www.digital-operational-resilience-act.com/Article_9.html Scope rationale:.
